title: Effort
takeaway: The goal comes to those who work for it and keep going, not to those who stop and rest.
scene: Four short four-line verses under the title 'Udham', meaning 'effort' or 'striving'. Each gives a small lesson about working hard, following your heart, and missing people.

original: جدوں کجھ سربند کر لین آہری
وگدے وین دریاواں دے رکدے نیں
transliteration: Jadon kujh sarband kar lain aahri
Vagde vain dariyaavaan de rukde nain
translation: When hard-working people make up their minds to do something,
even flowing rivers stop in their tracks.
couplets.story: When people who work hard decide to do something, they can achieve the impossible, even stopping a flowing river.

original: گھریں بیٹھیاں پند نہ مکدے نیں
transliteration: Ghareen baithiyaan pandh na mukde nain
translation: When you tie your belt and get ready, the goal comes near;
the journey never ends while you sit at home.
couplets.story: Once you roll up your sleeves and get going, the goal gets closer. But if you just sit at home, the journey never gets shorter.

original: منزل اس دے ہس کے پیر چمدی
جیہڑا ہس کے اوکڑاں سہہ جاندا
transliteration: Manzil us de has ke pair chumdi
Jehra has ke aukraan seh jaanda
translation: The goal happily kisses the feet of the one
who smiles and puts up with hardship.
couplets.story: The goal happily comes to people who face hard times with a smile.

original: راہی اوہ نہ منزل تے پج سکدا
چھاں رکھاں دی مانن جو بہہ جاندا
transliteration: Raahi oh na manzil te puj sakda
Chhaan rukkhaan di maanan jo beh jaanda
translation: That traveller can never reach the goal
who sits down to enjoy the shade of the trees.
couplets.story: A traveller who keeps stopping to rest in the shade will never arrive.

original: سدا جت ہوندی ایتھے جذبیاں دی
نری عقل تے سوچ بیکار ہوندی
transliteration: Sada jitt hondi ethe jazbiyaan di
Nari aql te soch bekaar hondi
translation: Here, it's always passion that wins;
mere cleverness and thinking are useless on their own.
couplets.story: In the end, it's people with passion and heart who win. Being clever isn't enough by itself.

original: عقلاں کنڈھے تے بہہ حیران ہوون
بناں جذبیوں نئیں بیڑی پار ہوندی
transliteration: Aqlaan kandhe te beh hairaan hovan
Binaan jazbiyon nahin beri paar hondi
translation: Reason sits on the riverbank, amazed:
without passion, no boat ever gets across.
couplets.story: The clever, careful people sit on the riverbank wondering how it's done. Without passion, no boat ever makes it to the other side.

original: دن لنگھدے جاندے گھٹ وٹ کے
transliteration: Din langhde jaande ghutt vatt ke
translation: The days pass by somehow, holding it in;
then the nights come and torment me.
couplets.story: During the day he manages to hold his feelings in. Then night comes, and the sadness hits.

original: ٹر جان والے بھل جان والے
transliteration: Tur jaan vaale, bhul jaan vaale
translation: Those who leave, those who forget,
and still the memories are yours, are theirs.
couplets.story: People leave, and people forget. The memories of them stay behind anyway.

deeper: The verse about passion (jazba) winning where reason stays on the bank echoes a Sufi theme found throughout the book. The heart, not cold calculation alone, carries you across, whether to a worldly goal or to God.
why: Short, quotable advice about effort and passion that would fit on a poster in any classroom.
prompt: What's a goal you've been 'sitting in the shade' on? What's one step you could take today?
notes: Four separate four-line verses: three on page 91 and one at the top of page 92.
The last verse (page 92) is about missing people rather than effort; it is grouped here because it has no title of its own.
